app.title: Browser tab title (HTML <title>) of web pages that don't set their own. The product name, Fivvi, the same in both languages.
app.name: Name of the native app under its home-screen icon (iOS CFBundleDisplayName and CFBundleName, Android app label). The name of the trainer app, Fivvi Pro, the same in both languages.
common.loading: Accessibility label of the progress indicator while a screen loads (read by VoiceOver and TalkBack).
common.loadingSlow: Line under a loading placeholder that is still waiting after 10 seconds.
common.retry: Button under an error message that tries the failed action again.
hello.greeting: Greeting above the home screen. {name} is the user's first name.
hello.sessionsToday: Number of sessions the trainer has today, 1 or more. For 0, use hello.noSessionsToday.
hello.nextSession: {date} is a weekday and date without year, e.g. 'dinsdag 22 september'. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '18:00'. Both are formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
hello.error: Shown on the native hello screen when the greeting can't be loaded (no connection, or an unknown greeting). Above the common.retry button.
home.setUpOnWeb: Native home when the account has no workspace but may set one up. Creating a workspace happens on the web only; this line tells the person to do that. Above home.openWeb.
home.openWeb: Button under home.setUpOnWeb in the native apps; opens Fivvi on the web (the first-run screen) in the phone's browser.
email.layout.footer: Last line of every email, below the content.
email.frame.clientReason: Footer line of every client email (the client frame, F049): why the person got it. {workspace} is the workspace's name as the owner typed it; do not change it.
email.frame.teamReason: Footer line of every email to a trainer or owner (the team frame, F049): why the person got it. {workspace} is the workspace's name as the owner typed it.
email.frame.questions: Footer line under the reason in client and team emails. {workspace} is the workspace's name: the person asks the gym, not Fivvi.
email.frame.button: Label of the one primary button of a client or team email; it opens the client web (fivvi.app).
email.frame.sentWith: Small last line at the bottom of client and team emails.
email.hello.subject: Subject of the test email that checks email delivery (E006). Only sent by the team, never to clients.
email.hello.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject.
email.hello.greeting: {firstName} is the recipient's first name. When unknown, use email.hello.greetingWithoutName.
email.hello.sentAt: {date} is a weekday and date with year, e.g. 'dinsdag 29 september 2026'. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '18:00'. Both are formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
email.signIn.subject: Subject of EM-08, the sign-in email. Contains the code and a sign-in link (inloglink).
email.signIn.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {code} is the 6-digit sign-in code.
email.signIn.intro: Line above the 6-digit sign-in code, which is shown on its own line below it.
email.signIn.linkIntro: Line above the sign-in link. The link opens a confirmation page; nothing is signed in until the person presses its button.
email.signIn.linkButton: Label of the button that opens the sign-in link (the confirmation page).
email.signIn.validity: {minutes} is how many minutes the code and the sign-in link work, e.g. 15.
email.signIn.ignore: Last line of the sign-in email, for someone who did not ask for it.
email.emailChangeCode.subject: Subject of EM-34, the email with the code that confirms a new email address (F005, spec #610). Sent to the NEW address only.
email.emailChangeCode.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {code} is the 6-digit code.
email.emailChangeCode.intro: Line above the 6-digit code, which is shown on its own line below it. The person asked to change the email address of their Fivvi account to this address.
email.emailChangeCode.validity: {minutes} is how many minutes the code works, e.g. 15. The second sentence says the new address is the one they sign in with from then on.
email.emailChangeCode.ignore: Last line, for someone who did not ask for it (a mistyped address, or somebody else's): the email changes nothing by itself.
signIn.title: Heading of the first step of the sign-in page (TW-10), where the email address is entered, and the browser tab title of the page.
signIn.emailLabel: Label of the email field on the sign-in page.
signIn.sendCode: Button under the email field of the sign-in page. Sends one email with a 6-digit code and a sign-in link.
signIn.checkEmailTitle: Heading of the second step of the sign-in page, shown after the email address was sent. Same wording whether or not the address has an account.
signIn.checkEmailBody: Under the heading of the second step. {email} is the address that was entered. Deliberately does not say whether an account exists (no account enumeration).
signIn.checkEmailBodyApp: Native apps only (TM-01): under the heading of the code step, instead of signIn.checkEmailBody. {email} is the address entered. Says the email has a code, without the sign-in link: a link tapped on the phone signs in the phone's browser, not the app. The instruction to enter the code comes from signIn.codeHelp. Deliberately does not say whether an account exists (no account enumeration).
signIn.codeLabel: Label of the field for the 6-digit code from the email (one-time-code autofill on phones). The word alone; the sentence is signIn.codeHelp.
signIn.codeHelp: Helper text under the code field on the second step of the sign-in page. The field is described by it.
signIn.submitCode: Button that signs in with the code that was entered.
signIn.resend: Button on the second step that sends a new email. The new code replaces the old one.
signIn.resent: Confirmation after a new email was requested. {email} is the address entered. Does not say whether an account exists.
signIn.changeEmail: Button on the second step that goes back to the email field.
signIn.confirmChecking: Shown for a moment on the confirm step (TW-10) while the page checks the sign-in link from the email. Checking uses nothing up.
signIn.confirmTitle: Heading of the confirm step, where the sign-in link from the email lands. {email} is the masked address the link signs in, e.g. j***@example.com.
signIn.confirmSubmit: The one button of the confirm step. Pressing it uses up the link and signs this browser in.
signIn.linkInvalidTitle: Heading of the confirm step when the link no longer works. One message for an expired, used or replaced link: it never says which.
signIn.linkInvalidBody: Line under signIn.linkInvalidTitle, pointing to the button that goes back to the sign-in page.
signIn.linkInvalidBack: Button on the confirm step for a link that no longer works. Goes back to the sign-in page, where a new email is requested.
signIn.signedOutNotice: Native apps only: notice at the top of the sign-in screen (TM-01) when the app was signed out without the person asking: the server no longer accepts the stored sign-in, or the person signed out elsewhere. Not shown after the person signs out in the app.
signIn.errors.invalidEmail: Under the email field when the address is empty or not an email address.
signIn.errors.invalidOrExpiredCode: Shown when the code was refused. One message for a wrong, expired, used or replaced code: it never says which.
signIn.errors.noConnection: Shown when the sign-in request could not reach the server.
signIn.errors.generic: Shown when sign-in failed for any other reason.
home.signedInAs: Native apps only: line on the signed-in home placeholder that says which account is signed in. {email} is the account's email address, shown in full to its owner.
welcome.title: Heading of TW-11, the first-run screen (`/welcome`) shown once to an operator-approved person who has no workspace yet. Fivvi is the product name.
welcome.description: Line under the heading of TW-11.
welcome.personNameLabel: Label of the field for the person's own name on TW-11. Shown only when the account has no name yet.
welcome.workspaceNameLabel: Label of the field for the name of the gym or business on TW-11. The workspace itself, worded as the person's own business (GLOSSARY §4.1: prefer this over the word werkruimte).
welcome.workspaceNameHint: Hint under the workspace name field on TW-11: an example of a name. "John's Gym" is a name, the same in both languages.
welcome.submit: Submit button of TW-11. It creates the workspace and opens it.
welcome.errors.personNameRequired: Under the name field on TW-11 when it is empty or only spaces.
welcome.errors.personNameTooLong: Under the name field on TW-11 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
welcome.errors.workspaceNameRequired: Under the workspace name field on TW-11 when it is empty or only spaces.
welcome.errors.workspaceNameTooLong: Under the workspace name field on TW-11 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
welcome.errors.noConnection: Shown on TW-11 when the request to create the workspace could not reach the server. Nothing was created.
welcome.errors.generic: Shown on TW-11 when creating the workspace failed for any other reason. Nothing was created.
noAccess.title: Heading of the no-access page: a signed-in person who is not in a workspace and may not create one (a client, or someone who was removed). The page has the sign-out button.
noAccess.body: Text of the no-access page (information-architecture §9.5, No permission). Native apps show it too, under the same conditions. The Dutch uses 'werkruimte' as the spec words it.
workspaceHome.description: Line under the workspace name on the placeholder home of a workspace, until the owner dashboard and the trainer's day arrive.
settingsGeneral.title: Heading and browser tab title of TW-08, Settings → General (`/w/{slug}/settings/general`, Owner only). Dutch: Algemeen.
settingsGeneral.nameLabel: Label of the workspace name field on TW-08. Same wording as the name field on the first-run screen.
settingsGeneral.save: Button of TW-08 that saves the new workspace name.
settingsGeneral.saved: Confirmation shown next to the save button on TW-08 after the name was saved.
settingsGeneral.urlNameLabel: Label of the read-only URL name of the workspace on TW-08 (the part of the web address and booking link made from the name at creation, which a rename never changes).
settingsGeneral.timeZoneLabel: Label of the read-only time zone of the workspace on TW-08, shown with its IANA name, e.g. Europe/Amsterdam.
settingsGeneral.errors.nameRequired: Under the name field on TW-08 when it is empty or only spaces.
settingsGeneral.errors.nameTooLong: Under the name field on TW-08 when the name is too long (the API refuses it: more than 80 characters).
settingsGeneral.errors.noConnection: Shown on TW-08 when the request to save could not reach the server. Nothing was changed.
settingsGeneral.errors.generic: Shown on TW-08 when saving failed for any other reason. Nothing was changed.
settingsLocation.title: Heading and browser tab title of TW-08, Settings → Location (`/w/{slug}/settings/locations`, Owner only). Dutch: Locatie (GLOSSARY §4.3).
settingsLocation.help: Help text under the heading of the location card on TW-08: every session and class takes the workspace's one location.
settingsLocation.nameLabel: Label of the location name field on TW-08. It is prefilled with the workspace name when the workspace is created.
settingsLocation.typeLabel: Label of the read-only location type on TW-08 (Eigen locatie / Own location).
settingsLocation.addressLegend: Legend of the group of address fields on TW-08 (postcode, house number, addition, street, city). Optional: an address is all or nothing.
settingsLocation.postcodeLabel: Label of the Dutch postcode field on TW-08, written like 1234 AB.
settingsLocation.houseNumberLabel: Label of the house number field on TW-08: one to five digits, no addition.
settingsLocation.additionLabel: Label of the optional house number addition field on TW-08, e.g. "A" or "2 hoog".
settingsLocation.streetLabel: Label of the street field on TW-08. The address lookup fills it in; the person can still type it.
settingsLocation.cityLabel: Label of the city field on TW-08. The address lookup fills it in; the person can still type it.
settingsLocation.save: Button of TW-08 that saves the location.
settingsLocation.saved: Confirmation shown next to the save button on TW-08 after the location was saved.
settingsLocation.lookup.busy: Shown on TW-08 while the street and city are looked up from the postcode and house number. The form stays usable.
settingsLocation.lookup.filled: Note on TW-08 under the address fields when the street and/or city were filled in by the address lookup.
settingsLocation.lookup.notFound: Shown on TW-08 when the lookup knows no address for the postcode and house number. Street and city stay empty for typing.
settingsLocation.lookup.unavailable: Shown on TW-08 when the address lookup timed out, failed or is used up for the hour. Saving a hand-typed address still works.
settingsLocation.types.organizationLocat: The type of the workspace's own location, shown read-only on TW-08 (GLOSSARY §4.3). The other types exist in the data model; they are not shown at go-live.
settingsLocation.errors.nameRequired: Under the name field on TW-08 when it is empty or only spaces.
settingsLocation.errors.nameTooLong: Under the name field on TW-08 when the name is over 120 characters. Same wording as the too-long workspace name.
settingsLocation.errors.postcodeInvalid: Under the postcode field on TW-08 when it is not a Dutch postcode (four digits, an optional space, two letters).
settingsLocation.errors.houseNumberInval: Under the house number field on TW-08 when it is not one to five digits.
settingsLocation.errors.tooLong: Under the addition, street or city field on TW-08 when the text is over its limit.
settingsLocation.errors.addressIncomplet: Under the address fields on TW-08 when some but not all of postcode, house number, street and city are filled in.
settingsLocation.errors.noConnection: Shown on TW-08 when the request to save could not reach the server. Nothing was changed.
settingsLocation.errors.generic: Shown on TW-08 when saving failed for any other reason. Nothing was changed.
workspaceNav.settingsLocation: Navigation link to Settings → Location (TW-08). Shown to the Owner only.
noPermission.title: Heading of the no-permission page (information-architecture §9.5): a team member opens a page their role may not use, such as a Trainer opening Settings.
noPermission.body: Text of the no-permission page. {workspace} is the name of the workspace, a name as typed by its owner and not translated.
workspaceNav.label: Accessible name of the navigation of a workspace's pages, read by screen readers.
workspaceNav.settings: Navigation link to Settings (Instellingen). Shown to the Owner only (GLOSSARY §4.8).
signOut.label: Button that signs out only the browser (or device) it is pressed on; other browsers stay signed in. On every signed-in page of the web app.
signOut.error: Shown next to the sign-out button when signing out failed (no connection or a server error). The person is still signed in and can try again.
userMenu.label: Accessible name of the button that opens the user menu (the ⋯ button) in the frame of a workspace's pages.
userMenu.language: Menu row that opens the two language options; {language} is the current language written in its own language (Nederlands or English).
userMenu.languageNl: Language option, always written in Dutch whatever the interface language (GLOSSARY §4.8).
userMenu.languageEn: Language option, always written in English whatever the interface language (GLOSSARY §4.8).
userMenu.error: Shown in the user menu when the chosen language could not be saved on the account (no connection or a server error). The page keeps its language and the person can try again.
userMenu.profile: Menu link to the page My profile (TW-09), where the person sees the workspaces they are on the team of.
roles.owner: Role label of an Owner (Eigenaar) of a workspace, shown as a plain label.
roles.trainer: Role label of a Trainer of a workspace, shown as a plain label.
workspaceSwitcher.newWorkspace: Last row of the scope switcher, only for accounts that may set up a workspace (the sign-up allowlist): opens the form to create another workspace. The + belongs to the label.
workspaceNav.workspaceWithRole: Header of the sidebar: the workspace name, then the role of the signed-in person in it, e.g. "John's Gym · Owner". {name} is the workspace name, {role} the role label.
myProfile.title: Title of the page My profile (TW-09).
myProfile.workspacesTitle: Heading of the section listing the workspaces the person is on the team of, each with their role.
myProfile.emailsTitle: Heading of the section of My profile (TW-09) with the switches for emails the person gets.
myProfile.bookingEmailsLabel: Label of the checkbox on My profile (TW-09) that switches the emails for a client booking or cancelling in the person's own classes on or off (F050). On by default; the setting belongs to the account.
workspaceNav.trainers: Navigation link to the Trainers page (TW-06), the team list. Shown to the Owner only.
team.title: Title of the Trainers page (TW-06), which lists the team of the workspace, and its browser tab title.
team.nameColumn: Column header of the person's name in the team list.
team.emailColumn: Column header of the email address in the team list.
team.roleColumn: Column header of the role label (Owner or Trainer) in the team list.
team.actionsColumn: Header of the last column of the team list, which holds the row action. Only read aloud by screen readers.
team.remove: Row action of a Trainer in the team list. Opens the remove dialog; the team access ends only after the Owner confirms there.
team.removeDialog.title: Title of the remove dialog, a question. {name} is the person's name (or email address when they have no name). No pronoun: the product does not know anyone's pronouns.
team.removeDialog.body: Body of the remove dialog. {name} is the person's name, repeated instead of a pronoun; {workspace} the workspace name. Says that only the team access goes and what they have as a client stays.
team.removeDialog.confirm: Destructive button of the remove dialog. Removes the person from the team.
team.removeDialog.cancel: Dismiss button of the remove dialog. Closes it without removing anyone.
team.removed: Confirmation shown after a person was removed from the team. {name} is the person's name (or email address when they have no name).
team.errors.noConnection: Shown on the Trainers page when removing a person failed because there is no connection. Nothing changed.
team.errors.generic: Shown on the Trainers page when removing a person failed for another reason. Nothing changed.
clients.title: Title of the clients list (TM-02, TW-01) and the label of the way in to it.
clients.newClient: Primary action of the native clients list (New client): opens the full-screen form that adds a client. Shown only to people who may manage clients.
clients.offline: Banner above the cached clients list in the apps while there is no connection. {time} is a 24-hour time, e.g. '08:42', formatted in code in the workspace time zone.
clients.addDialog.close: Accessibility label of the close button (x) of the new-client form in the apps.
clients.profile.back: Accessibility label of the back button of the client profile in the apps.
clients.profile.edit: Button on the client profile that opens the edit form for the overview (name, email address, language for emails).
clients.profile.editTitle: Title of the form that edits a client in the apps.
clients.profile.save: Button that saves the edited client.
clients.profile.saved: Brief confirmation (snackbar) after the edited client was saved.
common.cancel: Button that leaves a form or dialog without saving, e.g. the native full-screen dialog that changes the person's name.
myProfile.editName: Title of the native dialog (iOS sheet, Android full-screen dialog) in which the person changes their name on Profile (TM-04), and the action of the name row that opens it.
profile.support: Row on the native Profile (iOS and Android, F064 AC17) that opens the Help and contact page of the public website fivvi.app in the browser. Same wording as the website footer (site.footer.support).
profile.privacy: Row on the native Profile (iOS and Android, F064 AC17) that opens the privacy policy of the public website fivvi.app in the browser. Same wording as the website footer (site.footer.privacy).
profile.trainsHere.label: Label of the switch on the profile (web My profile TW-09, iOS and Android Profile TM-04), one per workspace where the person is Owner. On means they also train there and show as a trainer (F005). {workspace} is the workspace name, e.g. John's Gym. It talks about training, never about profiles.
profile.trainsHere.saved: Confirmation shown after the switch was saved.
profile.trainsHere.errors.noConnection: Shown next to the switch when saving failed because there is no connection. The switch is back as it was.
profile.trainsHere.errors.generic: Shown next to the switch when saving failed for another reason. The switch is back as it was.
team.badge.trainer: Badge on a team member of the Trainers page (TW-06) who trains in the workspace, next to their role label. The word for the role Trainer.
email.trainerInvitation.subject: Subject of EM-09, the email that invites a trainer to a workspace. {inviter} is the name of the Owner who invites, {workspace} the name of the workspace.
email.trainerInvitation.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {workspace} is the name of the workspace.
email.trainerInvitation.intro: The one sentence of EM-09. {inviter} is the name of the Owner who invites, {workspace} the name of the workspace; the person is invited to join its team as a trainer.
email.trainerInvitation.button: Label of the button that opens the invitation page, where the person accepts or declines.
email.trainerInvitation.validity: {date} is the last day the invitation works, a weekday and date with year, e.g. 'vrijdag 13 november 2026', in the workspace's time zone.
email.trainerInvitation.ignore: Last line of EM-09: the person can ignore the email when it is unexpected.
common.offline: Banner at the top of the client app while the phone has no connection. Not tied to one list, so it has no time (clients.offline names the time of a cached list).
profile.version: Line at the end of the client app's Profiel with the app's version. {version} is the version number, e.g. '0.1.0'.
clientNav.label: Accessibility label of the client app's tab bar (TalkBack).
clientNav.home: First tab of the client app. The same word in both languages (GLOSSARY: Home).
clientNav.book: Second tab of the client app: where a client books a class. A verb in the tab bar (GLOSSARY: Book / Boeken).
clientNav.profile: Third tab of the client app: the client's name, email address, language and sign-out.
noWorkspace.title: Client app, Home and Boeken while the client belongs to no workspace: tells them to ask their studio for the join link. The wording is marked in GLOSSARY.md until the pilot gym owner confirms.
noWorkspace.haveLink: Second line of the no-workspace state in the client app: the join link opens in the app when it is tapped on this phone.
noWorkspace.teamHint: Third line of the no-workspace state, only for an account that is Owner or Trainer of a workspace: points to the trainer app (Fivvi Pro).
email.privateSession.subject: Subject of EM-11, the email that confirms a new private session to the client. {date} is the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september', {time} the start time, e.g. '09:00'. 'Afspraak' is used in this subject only; everywhere else the product says 'privésessie'.
email.privateSession.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject. {date} is the weekday and date without year, {time} the start time.
email.privateSession.intro: First sentence of EM-11. {workspace} is the name of the workspace (the gym) where the session is planned.
email.privateSession.when: Line of EM-11 with the time of the session. {date} is the weekday and date with year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september 2026'; {start} and {end} are the start and end time, e.g. '09:00' and '10:00'.
email.privateSession.where: Line of EM-11 with the place. {location} is the name of the location, followed by its address when it has one.
email.privateSession.trainer: Line of EM-11 with the trainer. {trainer} is the trainer's name. Left out when the trainer has no name.
offers.summary.classesPerWeek: Part of the one-line summary of a membership: the classes a week. # is the number.
offers.summary.months: Part of an offer summary: a length in months (the term of a membership, the validity of a credit pack, the minimum term of a credit plan).
offers.summary.weeks: Part of the summary of a credit pack: a validity in weeks.
offers.summary.days: Part of the summary of a credit pack: a validity in days.
offers.summary.groupCredits: Part of an offer summary: a number of group credits.
offers.summary.privateCredits: Part of an offer summary: a number of private credits.
offers.summary.creditsEveryMonth: Part of the summary of a credit plan billed every month. {credits} is the number of credits, e.g. "4 privécredits".
offers.summary.creditsEveryFourWeeks: Part of the summary of a credit plan billed every 4 weeks. {credits} is the number of credits.
offers.summary.validFor: Part of the summary of a credit pack. {duration} is a length, e.g. "3 maanden".
offers.summary.minimumTerm: Part of the summary of a credit plan. {duration} is a length in months, e.g. "3 maanden".
offers.summary.pricePerMonth: Price of an offer billed every month. {amount} is the amount including VAT, e.g. "€ 79,00".
offers.summary.pricePerFourWeeks: Price of an offer billed every 4 weeks. {amount} is the amount including VAT.
offers.summary.singleClass: Part of the summary of a single class pass: what it is good for.
offers.cancellation.upTo: The cancellation rule as clients read it, for a cutoff of one hour or more. # is the number of hours.
offers.cancellation.untilStart: The cancellation rule as clients read it, for a cutoff of 0 hours.
email.privateSessionMoved.subject: Subject of EM-04, the email that tells the client a private session moved. {newDate} is the new day and time, built with email.privateSessionMoved.dateTime, e.g. 'vrijdag 25 september om 10:00'. Only the new date: with both the subject passed 78 characters (F049). Says 'sessie' here, as the spec words it; the UI says 'privésessie'.
email.privateSessionMoved.dateTime: A weekday, date and time inside the subject and the preview of EM-04. {date} is the weekday and date without year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september'; {time} the start time, e.g. '09:00'.
email.privateSessionMoved.preview: Preview text that inbox lists show next to the subject of EM-04. {newDate} is the new day and time, built with email.privateSessionMoved.dateTime.
email.privateSessionMoved.intro: First sentence of EM-04. {workspace} is the name of the workspace (the gym) where the session is planned.
email.privateSessionMoved.previously: Line of EM-04 with the time before the move. {date} is the weekday and date with year, e.g. 'donderdag 24 september 2026'; {start} and {end} are the start and end time.
email.privateSessionMoved.now: Line of EM-04 with the new time. {date} is the weekday and date with year; {start} and {end} are the start and end time.
